operator_io_quirks: Mixed-case table names (Student, Dorm, Dorm_amenity, Has_amenity, Lives_in) and mixed-case columns (StuID, LName, Fname, city_code, dormid, amenid, stuid, room_number) — must quote with original spelling, compare .lower().
DDL uses backtick-quoted FK parents (`Dorm`(dormid)) — sqlite_master text must be replayed verbatim; backticks are valid sqlite quoting.
Dorm, Dorm_amenity, Has_amenity, Lives_in have NO primary key (pk=[]); only Student has PK StuID. sample_fresh_primary_keys must no-op on empty PK.

All columns notnull=0 (declared nullable) and null_rate=0.0 in original — TS will still emit NULLs from empty-parent FK draws and String/Number samplers; inserts succeed since NOT NULL is not declared.

Dorm.dormid is INTEGER but NOT declared PK/UNIQUE — FK parents Dorm(dormid) and Dorm_amenity(amenid) are non-unique parents; TS draws with replacement so child FK values may repeat, fine for sqlite (no FK enforcement).
Has_amenity and Lives_in are pure junction tables with composite FKs and no PK — duplicate (dormid,amenid) / (stuid,dormid) rows are possible and legal.
Lives_in.stuid distinct=31 vs Student rows=34 — some students have no dorm; FK child draws from parent's FINAL filtered values, so orphan-free but not surjective.
VARCHAR(1) columns Sex and Dorm.gender: TS String fuzzer with length range from elements (len 1) — fresh strings will be 1 char from CHARSET, not restricted to {F,M,X}.
VARCHAR(3) city_code: TS String length range [3,4) from elements — fresh values are 3-char random strings, not IATA-like.
Dorm.gender has 3 distinct values (X,M,F) while Student.Sex has 2 (F,M) — no cross-table constraint; TS treats them independently.
All storage classes match declared types (integer/text) — no affinity contradictions to survive.
Tiny tables (7–40 rows): choose_table_sizes level-0 = 1+30u and x4 per level will produce instances far larger than originals; no huge-table sampling path exercised here.
operator_ts_expectations: Number fuzzer on StuID, Age, Major, Advisor, dormid, amenid, student_capacity, room_number: uniform in [-10^scale,10^scale] with scale=0 → integers in [-1,1] plus ±1/±2 perturbation; list range overwritten to full range (upstream quirk) → fresh draws cluster near 0, not near original 1001/600/900.
StuID is single-column PK → max_l0=inf, so fresh PK draws never reuse; but Number range [-1,1] means PKs collide heavily → sample_fresh_primary_keys drops most rows, shrinking Student drastically.

String fuzzer on LName/Fname/dorm_name/amenity_name: 5 sampled originals + pool literals, p=0.2 fresh random over a-zA-Z 0-9() with length from element lengths, then 50% contaminate (suffix/prefix/drop) → implausible names, likely FN source for name-equality predicates.
String on Sex/gender (len 1): fresh 1-char strings from full charset → 'F'/'M'/'X' predicates miss; FP risk when a random char coincidentally equals a queried value.
String on city_code (len 3): fresh 3-char strings, not real codes → city_code='BAL' style predicates mostly miss (FN).

FK columns (Has_amenity.dormid/amenid, Lives_in.stuid/dormid) draw from parent's final values with replacement → referential integrity holds but join cardinalities differ from original (Lives_in may have many rows per student).

Dorm and Dorm_amenity have no PK → no PK filtering; their dormid/amenid values come from Number sampler (near 0) while Has_amenity/Lives_in FK draws copy those same near-0 values → joins still match, but original 100/900 ranges lost.
No CHECK/UNIQUE constraints in DDL → drop_unique_duplicates is a no-op; all rows survive except PK-duplicate drops on Student.
Age/Major/Advisor near-0 values make range predicates (Age>20, Major=600) mostly false → FN; occasional ±1/±2 perturbation gives spurious matches → FP.
student_capacity near-0 vs original 85–400 → capacity comparisons (capacity>100) flip to mostly false.
No Date/Time/Bool/Bit columns → those fuzzers unused; no crash-fallback types (all dispatch cleanly to Number/String).
